title: EVA Foam vs Paperboard Inserts for a Diffuser Gift Set
seoTitle: EVA Foam vs Paperboard Inserts: Buyer Checks | MTT
summary: Compare EVA foam vs paperboard inserts for a diffuser gift set: support, removal, surface contact, assembly and the evidence to request before approval.
intro: Choose between EVA foam and paperboard inserts by defining what must stay in position, where the product can be supported and how it will be removed. Compare named material grades and complete structures, not just a soft sample against a stiff sheet. In MTT’s diffuser gift-box layout, the bottle and reed sticks occupy separate positions. That layout gives a useful starting point for an insert brief; the material choice needs the filled bottle, finished surfaces and intended shipping pack.
cta: Send the filled bottle dimensions and weight, reed bundle size, surface finishes, quantity and intended shipping arrangement. MTT can review an EVA and a folded-board proposal against the same fit and removal brief.
sections: Read the two product positions first

The MTT diffuser gift box places a short glass bottle beside a long reed bundle. The bottle cap and reed ends sit at different heights. Those differences matter before choosing a material: the bottle needs deliberate support, while the reed compartment needs to keep the bundle from migrating into the bottle space.

The visible cream surface does not identify the substrate underneath it. Use the pictured arrangement to discuss the geometry, then ask for a section drawing that names the insert material, facing and support below the bottle. A supplier should not quote EVA simply because the reference looks soft, or paperboard because its surface looks like paper.
Compare complete constructions, not material names

Two insert proposals for the same diffuser set
DecisionEVA foam proposalFolded paperboard proposal
Bottle locationCut cavity, depth and supporting baseCollars, folded supports and locking tabs
Product removalGrip opening and resistance at contact pointsFinger access without tearing a tab or lifting the deck
Surface contactFoam grade, exposed cut edges and any facingCut edges, coating and folded contact surfaces
Packing workLayers, bonding and placement in the boxErection sequence, locks and orientation
End of useIdentify foam, facing and adhesive separatelyIdentify board, coating and attached components separately

Compare both proposals inside the same outer box using the same filled bottle. Otherwise a thicker base, a changed cavity or a different outer carton can be mistaken for a benefit of the material alone.
Ask for a grade and the properties relevant to its job

Zotefoams’ Evazote material range provides grade-specific technical information. Use manufacturer data to identify a candidate, then request the actual supplier’s grade and test conditions. “EVA insert” alone does not specify compression behaviour, thickness or the way a laminated construction behaves.

For a board proposal, record the grade, thickness, grain direction and folded geometry. Holmen’s technical information distinguishes grammage, thickness and stiffness; they are not interchangeable specifications. A flat sheet comparison also misses what a folded wall or collar contributes.

Do not prescribe a universal cavity allowance from the bottle’s nominal width. Include dimensional variation, surface decoration, assembly and a practical removal check in the sample review. The custom insert purchasing page covers the information needed to start that discussion.
Keep the cap out of the load path

In this arrangement, the wooden-look cap is prominent and tempting to grip. Specify whether the user should lift the bottle by its body instead. A finger opening can provide access without making the entire cavity loose. Check the cap connection with the product supplier; packaging should not assume it can carry the filled bottle.

Load the finished bottle and inspect contact at the base, shoulder and decoration. Close the box with the actual reed bundle and any card in place. Look for cap pressure, reed movement and a deck that lifts when the bottle is removed. Record which component moved and why. These observations are more useful than describing a sample as simply too tight or too soft.
Separate presentation fit from transport protection

A neat recess can locate a bottle without providing enough protection for a parcel journey. Assess the presentation box, its insert, any void fill and the outer shipping carton as one pack. Define the transport route and relevant test plan before claiming protection.

If a foam proposal is intended to cushion impact, ask the engineer which material data, support area and loaded mass informed the design. If a board proposal depends on folded supports, check that they remain engaged after the agreed handling trial. Neither material name establishes a drop-test result.

Use the shipping outer-carton guide for the outer pack and the sample approval checklist to record the versions tested together.
Put the comparison into the quotation

Ask for separate material references, tooling, assembly work and sample charges for each proposal. Confirm whether an insert arrives flat, assembled or already fitted in the gift box. Include any facing and adhesive in the specification rather than leaving them hidden behind a unit price.

  • Keep the bottle, reed bundle and outer box versions identical across the comparison.
  • Record where each component is supported and how it is removed.
  • Photograph contact marks and any movement after the agreed checks.
  • Retain the accepted insert drawing and material reference for reorders.
  • Check local disposal routes before making a recyclability claim for the finished combination.

Choose the proposal that meets the documented brief. A lower material cost can be offset by packing work; an attractive facing can introduce a separate contact or sorting question. Neither needs a generic winner.

imageAlt: Violet MTT skincare shopping bag with pale stripes, cotton cord handles and a brown interior
title: CMYK vs Spot Colour Packaging: Specifying a Violet Retail Bag
seoTitle: CMYK vs Spot Colour Packaging: Proofing Guide | MTT
summary: Choose CMYK or spot colour for packaging using an MTT violet retail bag. Review artwork separations, paper, pale details and finished sample approval.
intro: For CMYK vs spot colour packaging, separate the artwork’s photographic content from the colours that must remain consistent across a range. CMYK suits multicolour images; a spot ink is a candidate for a critical solid brand colour. The choice still depends on the printer, paper and finish. MTT’s violet skincare bag makes the decision concrete: review the broad violet panels, narrow pale stripes and folded top as different checks, then approve a physical result rather than a screen colour.
cta: Send the editable artwork, brand colour reference, preferred paper, finish, quantities by design and the other packaging components that must match. MTT can help define the print route and sample approval record.
sections: Use the violet bag to identify the important colour areas

The MTT skincare duo bag combines broad violet panels, narrow light stripes and cord handles. Its brown interior is visible at the top. The artwork has two different risks: the large colour area makes variation noticeable, while the thin details need to remain clear after printing and folding.

The catalogue describes a two-colour print direction. That does not establish the final ink recipe, press or colour reference. Before requesting a production quotation, mark which colour is the brand priority and identify what the pale stripes should look like. A pale printed colour, an unprinted area and a metallic effect are different specifications.
Choose the printing route before converting the artwork

Adobe’s spot and process colour guidance distinguishes premixed spot inks from the four process inks: cyan, magenta, yellow and black. It also explains that the ink-and-paper combination affects a printed spot colour; its screen preview is not the physical result.

Artwork decisions to discuss with the printer
Artwork needRoute to compareApproval question
Product photographs or many coloursCMYK process reproductionWhich profile and proof represent the intended print condition?
One dominant solid brand colourA named spot-ink proposalHow does that ink appear on the selected paper?
Photos plus a critical brand solidProcess plus spot, if the printer supports itAre the extra separation and setup justified?
Metallic or selective surface effectA separately specified ink or finishing operationIs the approved effect included in the quotation?

Do not convert an approved spot separation to CMYK merely to make the file look simpler. Ask what the selected production process will actually output, then preserve that decision in the artwork instructions.
Resolve what sits beneath the pale stripes

Look closely at where a pale stripe crosses the violet field and approaches a fold. Specify whether the stripe is printed, left open to the paper colour or produced with a separate effect. Where the chosen substrate needs an opaque base to achieve the target appearance, ask the printer to include and sample it. Do not assume every press or paper combination behaves the same way.

Request the critical artwork area at final size. A reduced screen mockup hides the relationship between a narrow line and the printed background. Review the sample after conversion too: a stripe that appears even on a flat sheet may look different around a crease or glued joint.

The artwork preflight guide handles dielines and production layers. Here, the narrower decision is which colour separations and effects should survive that handoff.
Approve the paper and finish with the colour

A colour reference without a paper reference leaves too much open. Record the stock, surface and any coating or lamination. Compare the printed panel before and after the chosen finish, then retain the finished version as the approval reference.

When matching a bag to a rigid box, place the two physical components together. Their papers and finishes may differ even when the artwork uses the same colour name. Ask which component is the master reference and what variation is acceptable. Agree the viewing conditions and any measurement method before comparing readings; do not add a universal colour-difference limit to an order without discussing how it will be measured.

See custom paper bag specifications for the converted bag. The foil matching guide addresses a separate finishing decision.
Review separations, then review the physical sample

1. Identify the important solid colours and any images in the artwork.
  2. Agree whether each named colour remains a spot separation or is converted for the chosen process.
  3. Inspect the output preview for unintended extra colours, missing objects and overprint interactions.
  4. Approve the relevant printed proof or ink sample for its stated purpose.
  5. Review a converted, finished sample for folds, joins, rubbing and the relationship between panels.
  6. Record the artwork version, material and finish beside the signed approval.

A file check can confirm that a separation exists. It cannot show how the cord attachment, folded top or finished surface will look in use. Keep those acceptance checks in the sample record rather than treating one PDF approval as approval of every physical detail.
Keep repeat orders tied to the approved specification

For reorders, provide the approved physical reference and the production file version together. Confirm whether the paper, ink system or finishing process has changed. If one has changed, ask for a targeted comparison before authorising the full run.

Compare quotations on the same print route. Include setup, additional separations, any opaque base and finishing work where applicable. A short run with a large setup component has a different cost pattern from a repeat run, but the actual figures belong in the supplier’s itemised quote.

The aim is a reproducible purchasing specification: one identified violet reference, one agreed treatment for the pale detail and a finished bag sample that both sides can inspect. Record those decisions through the sample approval process.
